en: 50 g rolled oats
150 ml low-fat milk or yogurt
1 apple, grated
1 tbsp crushed almonds
1 tsp honey, lemon juice
Mix the oats with the milk in a bowl
Cover and refrigerate overnight
Grate the apple and sprinkle it with lemon so it does not brown
Stir it into the oats, add the honey and almonds
2 slices wholegrain rye bread
100 g low-fat quark
Fresh herbs (chives, dill, parsley)
1 small garlic clove, crushed
Cucumber and radish slices, salt, pepper
Chop the herbs finely
Mix them into the quark with the garlic, salt and pepper
Let it sit 10 minutes so the flavours mingle
Spread on the bread and top with cucumber and radish

name.en: Soft-Boiled Egg with Wholegrain Bread and Butter

en: 2 eggs
2 slices whole-wheat bread (60 g)
Low-fat butter 1 tsp
Salt and black pepper
Chopped chives for garnish (optional)
Cherry tomatoes to serve (optional)
Place the eggs in boiling water and cook for exactly 6-7 minutes for a soft, runny centre.
Remove the eggs and place in cold water for a few seconds to make peeling the top easier.
Peel just the top and leave the egg in its shell in an egg cup, sprinkle with salt and black pepper.
Butter the bread and serve with the egg and cherry tomatoes, sprinkle with chives if desired.

name.en: Bauernfrühstück (German Farmer's Breakfast with Potatoes and Eggs)

en: Boiled potatoes, cubed, 150 g
2 eggs
Lean bacon or ham, chopped, 40 g
1 small onion, chopped
Chopped chives for garnish
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
Heat the oil and brown the onion and boiled potatoes for 7-8 minutes over medium heat until the edges turn golden.
Add the bacon and stir for 3 minutes until lightly toasted.
Beat the eggs with salt and black pepper and pour over the mixture, gently stir 3-4 minutes until the egg sets.
Sprinkle with chives and serve hot.

name.en: Quark with Oats, Honey and Berries

en: Low-fat quark 150 g
Oats 2 tbsp
Honey 1 tsp
Mixed fresh or frozen berries 60 g
A pinch of ground cinnamon (optional)
1 tsp chopped walnuts for garnish (optional)
Put the quark in a serving bowl and stir until smooth.
Add the oats and mix well.
Distribute the berries over it, add the honey and cinnamon if desired.
Sprinkle with chopped walnuts, and serve immediately or chill for 10 minutes to soften the oats slightly.

name.en: German Scrambled Eggs with Tomato and Marjoram on Dark Bread

en: 2 eggs
1 medium tomato, chopped
Dried marjoram half a tsp (or thyme as a substitute)
1 slice dark rye bread (40 g)
1 tsp low-fat butter
Salt and black pepper
Beat the eggs with salt and black pepper.
Heat a non-stick pan and sauté the tomato for two minutes until slightly softened.
Add the beaten egg and marjoram, stir constantly until the egg sets and becomes crumbly.
Butter the bread and serve with the scrambled eggs.

name.en: Milchreis (German Rice Pudding) with Cinnamon and Apple

en: Short-grain white rice 40 g
Low-fat milk 300 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp and a pinch of salt
1 small apple, cubed
Ground cinnamon
Sliced almonds for garnish (optional)
Wash the rice thoroughly and place it with the milk and salt in a pot.
Cook over very low heat 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rice is cooked and the texture becomes creamy.
Add the brown sugar and chopped apple and cook 5 more minutes until the apple softens.
Pour into a serving bowl, sprinkle with cinnamon and almonds, and serve warm.

name.en: Wholegrain Roll with Honey and Walnuts

en: Wholegrain bread roll or thick slice 70 g
Low-fat cream cheese 2 tbsp
Honey 1 tsp
Coarsely chopped walnuts 1 tbsp
A pinch of ground cinnamon (optional)
Sliced apple to serve (optional)
Cut the bread in half if using a roll.
Spread it generously with the cream cheese.
Drizzle the honey evenly over it.
Scatter the chopped walnuts over the honey, sprinkle with cinnamon if desired, and serve with apple slices.

name.en: Pumpernickel Bread with Cream Cheese and Grapes

en: Pumpernickel bread (dark rye), 2 slices (60 g)
Low-fat cream cheese 40 g
Green or red grapes, half a cup (50 g)
Chopped walnuts for garnish (optional)
A little honey for garnish (optional)
A pinch of chia seeds (optional)
Spread the pumpernickel slices generously with cream cheese.
Halve the grapes and arrange them over the cheese.
Sprinkle with chopped walnuts if desired.
Drizzle with a little honey and chia seeds for garnish, and serve immediately.

name.en: Haferbrei (German Oat Porridge) with Cinnamon and Pear

en: Oats 40 g
Low-fat milk 200 ml
1 small pear, cubed
Ground cinnamon and brown sugar 1 tsp
A pinch of salt
Sliced almonds for garnish (optional)
Put the oats, milk and salt in a small pot.
Cook over low heat 7-8 minutes, stirring, until the texture becomes creamy.
Add the chopped pear and brown sugar and cook 3 more minutes until the pear softens slightly.
Pour into a serving bowl, sprinkle with cinnamon and almonds, and serve warm.
120 g brown lentils
1 carrot, 1 celery stick, 1 onion, 1 potato
1 tsp oil
Bay leaf, apple vinegar
Salt, pepper, marjoram
Sauté the onion, carrot and celery in the oil 5 minutes
Add the lentils, potato, bay leaf and 5 cups of water
Simmer 35 minutes until the lentils are tender
Stir in the vinegar and seasoning at the end
300 g small boiled potatoes
Half cup warm vegetable stock
1 tsp mustard
1 tbsp oil, 2 tbsp vinegar
1 onion, chives, pickled cucumber
Peel the warm potatoes and slice them
Whisk the warm stock with mustard, vinegar, oil and salt
Pour the dressing over the potatoes while warm so they absorb it
Add the onion and pickle, rest 30 minutes before serving
Potato, cubed, 200 g
Carrot and celery, chopped, 60 g
1 medium onion
Lean sausage, sliced, 40 g
Light vegetable stock 400 ml
1 tbsp light cream and chopped parsley for garnish
Sauté the onion, carrot and celery in a dry pan for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the potato and vegetable stock, cover and simmer over medium heat 18-20 minutes until the potato is fully tender.
Blend a third of the soup with an immersion blender to give it a thicker texture while keeping some chunks.
Add the sausage and cook 5 more minutes, drizzle with the light cream and garnish with parsley, and serve hot.

name.en: Flammkuchen (Thin Flatbread with Crème Fraîche and Onion)

en: Ready-made thin whole-wheat pizza dough 100 g
Low-fat crème fraîche or sour cream 60 g
1 large onion, very thinly sliced
Lean bacon, chopped, 30 g
Nutmeg, salt and black pepper
Chopped parsley for garnish (optional)
Roll out the dough very thin on a lined tray.
Mix the sour cream with the nutmeg, salt and black pepper, spread it thinly over the dough.
Distribute the onion and bacon evenly over the cream.
Bake at 230°C for 12-15 minutes until the edges are golden and crisp, sprinkle with parsley and serve hot.

name.en: Light German Goulash with Beef and Dark Bread

en: Lean beef, small cubes, 120 g
Red bell pepper and 1 large onion
Puréed tomato 100 g
Sweet paprika 1 tbsp and a pinch of caraway
Light vegetable stock 250 ml
1 slice dark bread (40 g) to serve
Brown the onion and bell pepper in a dry pan for 5 minutes until softened.
Add the beef and stir until it changes colour.
Add the paprika and caraway and stir for a minute, then add the tomato and stock.
Cover and simmer 45-50 minutes until the beef is tender and the texture thickens, and serve with the dark bread.
Cooked whole-wheat pasta 100 g
Red bell pepper, sweetcorn and cucumber, chopped, 150 g total
Lean turkey ham, chopped, 50 g
Low-fat yogurt 2 tbsp and low-fat mayonnaise 1 tbsp for the dressing
Mild mustard half a tsp and vinegar 1 tsp
Salt, black pepper and chopped parsley for garnish
Mix the yogurt, mayonnaise, mustard, vinegar, salt and black pepper to make the dressing.
Put the cooked pasta in a large bowl.
Add the bell pepper, sweetcorn, cucumber and turkey ham.
Add the dressing and toss well, chill for 15 minutes, garnish with parsley and serve cold.

name.en: Erbsensuppe (German Split Pea Soup with Sausage)

en: Split yellow peas 60 g
Carrot and celery, chopped, 60 g
1 medium onion
Lean sausage, sliced, 40 g
Light vegetable stock 400 ml
Chopped parsley for garnish, salt and black pepper
Soak the peas for an hour if possible, then drain.
Brown the onion, carrot and celery in a dry pot for 4 minutes until softened.
Add the peas and vegetable stock, cover and simmer 35-40 minutes until the peas fully break down and the texture thickens.
Add the sausage and cook 5 more minutes, adjust the salt and black pepper, garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name.en: Bunter Salat (Mixed Salad with Egg and Ham)

en: Chopped lettuce, tomato and cucumber, 150 g total
1 boiled egg, quartered
Lean turkey ham, cubed, 40 g
Low-fat grated cheese 20 g
Olive oil 1 tsp and vinegar 1 tsp
Mild mustard half a tsp, salt and black pepper
Arrange the lettuce, tomato and cucumber on a serving plate.
Add the ham and grated cheese on top.
Place the boiled egg quarters on top.
Mix the olive oil, vinegar, mustard, salt and black pepper, drizzle over the salad and serve immediately.
Lean beef, small cubes, 100 g
Potato, carrot and celery, chopped, 200 g total
1 medium onion and 1 crushed garlic clove
A bay leaf and light vegetable stock 400 ml
Chopped parsley for garnish
Salt and black pepper
Brown the onion and garlic in a dry pot for 3 minutes.
Add the beef and stir until it changes colour.
Add the potato, carrot, celery, bay leaf and stock.
Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes until the beef is tender and the vegetables are cooked, adjust the salt and black pepper, garnish with parsley and serve hot.

name.en: Brotzeit-Teller (German Cold Cuts and Cheese Platter)

en: Rye bread, 2 slices (70 g)
Lean turkey ham 50 g
Low-fat cheese, sliced, 40 g
2 small pickled cucumbers
Cherry tomatoes and radishes, 100 g total
Mild mustard to serve
Arrange the bread slices on a serving plate.
Place the ham and cheese slices on or beside the bread.
Arrange the pickles, cherry tomatoes and radishes around the plate.
Serve with the mustard on the side for dipping.
170 g turkey breast, pounded thin
1 egg
30 g wholewheat breadcrumbs
1 tbsp grated parmesan
1 tsp oil, lemon, parsley
Mix the breadcrumbs with parmesan, salt and pepper
Dip the meat in the egg, then in the crumb mixture
Place on baking paper and spray or drizzle with the oil
Bake 20 minutes at 200°C and serve with lemon
4 large cabbage leaves
150 g lean minced meat
30 g oats or breadcrumbs
1 onion, 1 egg, marjoram
1 cup stock, 1 tsp oil
Blanch the cabbage leaves 2 minutes until pliable
Mix the meat with oats, egg, onion and marjoram
Fill the leaves, roll them and tie with kitchen string
Brown them in the oil, add the stock and cook 40 minutes

name.en: Sauerbraten (German Marinated Pot Roast) with Potatoes

en: Lean beef, large cubes, 140 g
Apple cider vinegar 2 tbsp and water 150 ml for marinating
Bay leaves, 2 cloves and 1 medium onion, sliced
Chopped carrot 50 g
Raisins 1 tbsp (traditional, optional)
Boiled potatoes 150 g to serve
Marinate the beef with the apple cider vinegar, water, bay leaves, cloves and onion, cover and refrigerate 4-6 hours or overnight.
Remove the beef from the marinade and reserve the liquid, heat a dry pan and brown the beef on all sides for 5 minutes.
Add the strained marinade liquid, carrot and raisins, cover and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes until the beef is fully tender.
Mash some of the carrot to thicken the sauce if desired, and serve with the boiled potatoes.

name.en: Königsberger Klopse (Meatballs in Caper Sauce) with Potatoes

en: Lean minced beef 140 g
1 small grated onion and 1 egg
Fine breadcrumbs 2 tbsp
Light vegetable stock 300 ml
Drained capers 1 tbsp and low-fat yogurt 2 tbsp for the sauce
1 tsp cornflour and boiled potatoes 150 g to serve
Knead the minced beef with the grated onion, egg, breadcrumbs and salt until it binds together.
Shape into medium-sized balls.
Bring the vegetable stock to a boil in a wide pot, add the meatballs and simmer 15-18 minutes until fully cooked, remove and set aside, keeping the broth.
Dissolve the cornflour in a little water, add it to the broth with the capers and yogurt, cook 3-4 minutes until the sauce thickens, pour it over the meatballs and serve with the potatoes.

serving.en: 1 plate with potatoes and cabbage (~400 g)

name.en: Baked Schweinebraten (German Roast Pork) with Potatoes and Red Cabbage

en: Flattened lean pork or turkey 140 g
2 crushed garlic cloves and ground caraway
Salt and black pepper
Grated red cabbage 150 g and 1 small grated apple
Apple cider vinegar 1 tsp and a pinch of cinnamon for the cabbage
Boiled potatoes 150 g to serve
Rub the meat with the crushed garlic, caraway, salt and black pepper, let it sit 15 minutes.
Arrange on a lined tray and bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes depending on thickness until fully cooked.
Meanwhile, cook the red cabbage with the grated apple, apple cider vinegar and cinnamon in a pan over medium heat 15 minutes until softened.
Serve the meat with the cabbage and boiled potatoes.

name.en: Baked Fischfrikadellen (German Fish Cakes) with Potatoes

en: Chopped white fish fillet 150 g
1 small chopped onion and 1 egg
Fine breadcrumbs 2 tbsp and chopped parsley
Mild mustard half a tsp, salt and black pepper
1 tsp oil for brushing
Boiled potatoes 150 g and lemon to serve
Mix the chopped fish with the onion, egg, breadcrumbs, parsley, mustard, salt and black pepper until well combined.
Shape the mixture into medium-sized patties with your hands.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush both sides with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and fully cooked, and serve with the boiled potatoes and lemon slices.

name.en: Rinderrouladen (Beef Roulade with Bacon and Pickle) with Potatoes

en: Thin lean beef slices 140 g
Mild mustard 1 tsp for spreading
Lean bacon, sliced, 20 g
Pickled cucumber, cut into sticks, and 1 small onion, sliced
Light vegetable stock 200 ml
Boiled potatoes 150 g to serve
Lay out the beef slices and spread with mustard.
Arrange the bacon, pickle and onion along each slice.
Roll tightly and secure with toothpicks or kitchen string.
Heat a dry pan and brown the rolls on all sides for 5 minutes, add the stock, cover and simmer 50-60 minutes until fully tender, and serve with the potatoes.

name.en: Baked Herring Fillets with Potatoes and Mustard Sauce

en: Herring or white fish fillet 140 g
Mild mustard 2 tbsp
Low-fat yogurt 2 tbsp for the sauce
Chopped spring onion and a little lemon juice
Boiled potatoes 150 g
Chopped parsley for garnish, salt and black pepper
Season the fish fillet with salt and black pepper.
Brush with one tablespoon of the mustard and arrange on a lined tray.
Bake at 200°C for 15-18 minutes until cooked and it flakes easily.
Mix the remaining mustard with the yogurt, spring onion and lemon juice, serve as a side sauce with the fish and boiled potatoes.

name.en: Senfeier (Eggs in German Mustard Sauce) with Potatoes

en: 2 boiled, peeled eggs
Whole-wheat flour 1 tbsp
Low-fat milk 200 ml
Mild mustard 2 tbsp
1 tsp low-fat butter
Boiled potatoes 150 g and chopped parsley for garnish
Melt the butter in a small pot over low heat, add the flour and stir for a minute.
Gradually add the milk, stirring constantly, until the texture thickens without lumps.
Add the mustard and cook 2 more minutes until the sauce is smooth.
Halve the eggs and place them in the sauce, cook for a minute to warm through, garnish with parsley and serve with the boiled potatoes.

name.en: Pan-Seared Salmon with German Dill Sauce and Potatoes

en: Salmon fillet 140 g
Salt, black pepper and 1 tsp oil
Low-fat yogurt 2 tbsp for the sauce
Chopped fresh dill 2 tbsp
Lemon juice 1 tsp and mild mustard half a tsp
Boiled potatoes 150 g to serve
Season the salmon with salt and black pepper.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, cook the salmon skin-side down 4 minutes until crisp, flip and cook 3 more minutes.
Mix the yogurt, dill, lemon juice and mustard to make the sauce.
Serve the salmon with the dill sauce and boiled potatoes.
150 g low-fat quark
Half cup berries or chopped fruit
1 tsp honey
1 tsp flaxseed
A dash of vanilla
Whisk the quark with the honey and vanilla until smooth
Fold in half the fruit gently
Spoon it into a small cup
Top with the remaining fruit and the flaxseed
50 g wholewheat bread dough
1 tsp caraway seeds
A pinch of coarse salt
Carrot, cucumber, pepper sticks
1 tbsp quark for dipping
Roll the dough into thin sticks
Sprinkle with caraway and salt and press them in gently
Bake 12 minutes at 200°C until crisp
Serve with the vegetable sticks and quark
Whole-wheat flour 80 g
Instant yeast half a tsp
Warm water 45 ml and a little salt for the dough
Baking soda 1 tbsp and water 500 ml for the quick boil
Coarse salt for topping (a small amount)
1 beaten egg for brushing
Knead the flour with the yeast, warm water and salt to a cohesive dough, let it rest 45 minutes until it doubles in size.
Shape the dough into a long rope and twist it into the traditional pretzel shape.
Boil the water with the baking soda, dip the pretzel in it for just 20 seconds, then remove with a slotted spoon.
Place on a lined tray, brush with the beaten egg, sprinkle with coarse salt, and bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes until golden.

name.en: Vegetable Sticks with Herb Quark Dip

en: Low-fat quark or Greek yogurt 100 g
Chopped parsley, chives and dill 2 tbsp
Lemon juice 1 tsp, salt and black pepper
Carrot, cucumber and bell pepper, in strips, 150 g total
1 very small crushed garlic clove (optional)
Mix the quark with the chopped herbs, lemon juice, salt and black pepper.
Add the crushed garlic if desired and mix well.
Chill the dip for 10 minutes to firm up and let the flavours meld.
Cut the vegetables into long sticks, arrange on a serving plate with the dip, and serve immediately.
Grated potato, squeezed of liquid, 200 g
1 small grated onion
1 egg
2 tbsp whole-wheat flour
Salt and a pinch of nutmeg
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the squeezed potato with the onion, egg, flour, salt and nutmeg until well combined.
Spoon the mixture into flat mounds on a lined tray.
Brush the tops with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

name.en: Radish and Cream Cheese Open Sandwich

en: 1 slice rye bread (40 g)
Low-fat cream cheese 30 g
6 thinly sliced radishes
Chopped chives and a little salt
Sesame seeds or nigella seeds for garnish (optional)
Chopped parsley (optional)
Spread the bread with a thick layer of cream cheese.
Arrange the radish slices over the cheese in an attractive overlap.
Sprinkle with a little salt and the chives.
Garnish with sesame seeds or parsley if desired, and serve immediately.
Spätzle (small German noodles) or short whole-wheat pasta 100 g
1 medium onion, thinly sliced
Low-fat grated cheese 40 g
Low-fat yogurt 2 tbsp
1 tsp oil, salt and black pepper
Chopped parsley for garnish
Boil the spätzle according to package instructions, drain.
Brown the onion in a dry pan for 6-7 minutes until golden.
Mix the spätzle with the onion, yogurt, salt and black pepper in an oven-safe dish.
Sprinkle the grated cheese on top, bake at 200°C for 12-15 minutes until the cheese melts and turns slightly crisp, garnish with parsley and serve hot.
Whole-wheat flour 60 g
Low-fat grated cheese 40 g
Cold low-fat butter 2 tsp
About 2 tbsp cold water
A little salt and a pinch of ground caraway
Sesame seeds for garnish (optional)
Mix the flour with the grated cheese, salt and caraway.
Add the cold butter and rub it into the flour with fingertips until the texture resembles crumbs.
Gradually add the cold water and knead quickly until a cohesive dough forms.
Roll it out very thin, cut into small squares, sprinkle with sesame if desired, and bake at 190°C for 12-15 minutes until golden and crisp.
3 medium carrots (250 g)
1 tsp olive oil
A little salt
A pinch of sweet paprika (optional)
A pinch of ground caraway (optional)
A little lemon juice (optional)
Peel the carrots and slice them very thinly with a peeler or mandoline.
Put the slices in a bowl, sprinkle with the oil, salt, paprika and caraway if desired, toss well until evenly coated.
Arrange in a single layer on a lined tray without overlapping.
Bake at 160°C for 20-25 minutes, watching closely toward the end, until golden and crisp, let cool slightly as they crisp up further, and sprinkle with lemon juice if desired before serving.
Lean minced beef 140 g
1 small finely chopped onion and 1 small crushed garlic clove
Fine breadcrumbs 2 tbsp and 1 egg
Mild mustard half a tsp and chopped parsley
Salt, black pepper and a pinch of ground caraway
1 tsp oil for brushing
Knead the minced meat with the onion, garlic, breadcrumbs, egg, mustard, parsley, salt, black pepper and caraway until it binds together.
Shape into small flat, bite-sized balls.
Arrange on a lined tray and brush both sides with oil.
Bake at 220°C for 15-18 minutes, turning halfway, until fully cooked and golden.
3 apples, peeled and chopped
3 tbsp water
1 cinnamon stick
A few drops of lemon juice
1 tsp honey (optional)
Put the apple, water and cinnamon stick in a pot
Cover and cook 15 minutes on low heat
Remove the cinnamon and mash the apple with a fork
Add lemon and honey, serve warm or cold
200 g mixed red berries
150 ml cherry juice or water
1 tbsp cornstarch
1 tsp honey
1 tbsp yogurt to serve
Heat the juice with the honey until it boils
Dissolve the cornstarch in 2 tbsp of cold water
Stir it into the juice until it thickens
Add the berries, cook 2 minutes, chill and serve with yogurt
2 medium apples, peeled and chopped (250 g)
Raisins 1 tbsp and ground cinnamon
Brown sugar 2 tsp and a little lemon juice
Filo pastry, 3 sheets (50 g)
Fine breadcrumbs 1 tbsp to absorb moisture
2 tsp melted butter for brushing
Mix the chopped apples with the raisins, cinnamon, brown sugar and lemon juice.
Lay out a filo sheet and brush with the butter, sprinkle a little breadcrumb, repeat with the other two sheets layering on top.
Place the apple mixture along the edge of the dough, roll it tightly into a log, place seam-side down on a lined tray.
Brush with the remaining butter and bake at 200°C for 25-30 minutes until golden and crisp, let cool slightly before slicing.
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
2 eggs
Low-fat milk 80 ml
Brown sugar 1 tsp and a pinch of salt
Mixed fresh or frozen berries 80 g
A light dusting of icing sugar for garnish, and 1 tsp oil
Beat the eggs with the milk, brown sugar and salt, gradually add the flour until it becomes a smooth, lump-free batter.
Heat the oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, pour in the batter and spread it out.
Cook 3-4 minutes until the bottom sets, flip and cook 2 more minutes.
Use two forks to tear the pancake into irregular pieces in the pan, add the berries and gently toss for a minute, dust lightly with icing sugar and serve hot.
Low-fat quark 150 g
1 egg
Whole-wheat flour 40 g
Brown sugar 2 tsp and grated lemon zest
A quarter tsp baking powder and a pinch of salt
1 tsp oil for brushing
Mix the quark with the egg, brown sugar and lemon zest until combined.
Add the flour, baking powder and salt, mix until a soft dough forms.
Shape into small flat balls with wet hands, arrange on a lined tray.
Brush the tops with oil and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes, turning halfway, until golden.
Fresh or frozen rhubarb, chopped, 200 g
Brown sugar 30 g
Water 2 tbsp
A little grated orange zest (optional)
1 small cinnamon stick (optional)
Fresh mint for garnish (optional)
Put the rhubarb in a pot with the brown sugar, water, orange zest and cinnamon stick.
Cover and simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the rhubarb softens and the texture thickens slightly.
Remove the cinnamon stick, let the compote cool slightly.
Serve warm or cold, garnish with fresh mint if desired.

name.en: Baked Bienenstich (Bee Sting Cake with Honey and Almonds)

en: Whole-wheat flour 50 g and instant yeast a quarter tsp
Warm low-fat milk 40 ml
1 egg
Sliced almonds 25 g and honey 2 tbsp for the topping
1 tsp low-fat butter
Low-fat quark 60 g for a light filling (optional)
Knead the flour with the yeast, warm milk and egg to a soft dough, let it rest 45 minutes.
Spread it into a small greased tin, let the dough rest another 10 minutes.
Heat the honey with the butter and almonds in a small pan for two minutes, spread evenly over the dough.
Bake at 180°C for 20-22 minutes until the almonds are golden and the base is set, let cool completely, then slice horizontally and fill with the quark if desired before serving.
Whole-wheat flour 50 g
Instant yeast a quarter tsp
Warm low-fat milk 40 ml
Fresh plums, pitted and halved, 150 g
Brown sugar 2 tsp and ground cinnamon
1 tsp low-fat butter for brushing
Knead the flour with the yeast and warm milk to a soft dough, let it rest 45 minutes.
Spread it into a small tin greased with butter.
Arrange the plum halves over the dough in an overlapping pattern, sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until the plums are cooked and the dough edges turn golden, let cool slightly before serving.
Low-fat milk 250 ml
Cornflour 2 tbsp
Brown sugar 2 tsp
Vanilla extract 1 tsp
Mixed fresh or frozen berries 60 g
A pinch of salt
Dissolve the cornflour in a quarter cup of cold milk until smooth without lumps.
Heat the remaining milk with the brown sugar and salt until near boiling.
Gradually stir in the cornflour mixture, stirring constantly, and cook 3-4 minutes until the texture thickens like pudding.
Remove from the heat and add the vanilla, pour into serving cups, chill for at least an hour, and garnish with berries before serving.
Ground poppy seeds 40 g
Whole-wheat flour 30 g
1 egg
Low-fat milk 50 ml
Brown sugar 2 tsp and grated lemon zest
A quarter tsp baking powder and 1 tsp oil for greasing
Beat the egg with the brown sugar and lemon zest until the mixture becomes pale.
Add the milk and mix.
Mix the ground poppy seeds with the flour and baking powder, gradually add to the egg mixture until the batter is combined.
Pour into a small tin greased with oil, bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until cooked and it springs back when pressed gently, let cool before slicing.
